$comment: Praxis operational failure boundaries (SAF-AEGIS-1). Expected outcomes (refused transitions, failed verification, stale installation state, user-owned-file conflicts, unsupported commands, policy refusals) stay typed Praxis/Ordo results with documented exit codes and are not Aegis faults (SAF-AEGIS-2). Classification lives in src/Praxis.Infrastructure/Boundary/AegisBoundary.fs; tests/Praxis.Tests/AegisBoundaryTests.fs asserts these codes equal the module's.

boundaries.name: Command line
boundaries.$comment: Every command runs inside one Aegis capture. A failure that escapes is attributed to the adapter boundary that raised it: thrown from Praxis.Infrastructure.Git is GIT; network, process, filesystem and repository-state failures by type; anything else is CLI.UNEXPECTED. Programming defects and cancellation are re-raised.

boundaries.name: Web and hub request handling
boundaries.$comment: praxis web serve and praxis hub serve capture each request and each connection. A fault is answered with HTTP 500, the safe message and an AG- reference; the exception text never reaches the browser.

rules: praxis-work-content (description, content, prompt, transcript, body, title, attachment, note, evidence)
redaction.technicalDetails: Credentials in exception text (URL user-info, GitHub tokens, bearer/basic headers, token=/password=/secret= values) are replaced with [redacted] before the fault is recorded.
redaction.context: Only the command words are public; the repository root is sensitive and masked.

persistence.fallbackBehaviour: Delivery is awaited (Blocking) so a record cannot lose the race with process exit; a sink failure is written to standard error.
persistence.retentionPolicy: No durable Aegis sink is configured; the standard-error sink is the record.
